title: A History of India
description:
S01 E03 — Indus Valley Civilization
Turning to the urban people of the Indus Valley; many mysteries abound regarding this long-lost Bronze Age civilization; exploring excavated cities; examining art and artifacts; what people know about this society; what may have happened to them.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E04 — Indo-European Vedic Culture
Exploring the ancient foundations of Hinduism, which emerge from people who identify themselves with the Vedas; studying these poems and hymns; the civilization's culture and cosmology; the origins and development of the Indo-European language.

title: Renaissance: The Transformation of the West
description:
S01 E01 — The Spirit of Renaissance
Learning how the Renaissance pioneers a new way of thinking about history itself; exploring who, exactly, the typical Renaissance man is; getting answers to the questions about the Renaissance's powerful fusion of classical and medieval worldviews.

title: Renaissance: The Transformation of the West
description:
S01 E02 — Rebirth: Classical Values Made New
Considering how the key contexts and values of the European Renaissance set the stage for a new era of questions, the two chief examples to chart the origins of the European Renaissance are the Black Death and the letters of Petrarch.

title: Renaissance: The Transformation of the West
description:
S01 E03 — The Medieval Roots of Italian Renaissance
The Renaissance first blooms in Italy; the politics and economics of medieval Italian states; the legacies of antiquity gain traction throughout the peninsula; the influence of trade revivals, a dynamic social order and the profits from holy wars.

title: Renaissance: The Transformation of the West
description:
S01 E04 — The Rise of the Humanists
Focusing on humanism, one of the most challenging foundational concepts of the Renaissance; how and why education undergoes its extreme makeover; exploring the fields that dominate this new way of learning; humanist schools and schoolmasters.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E01 — The Interconnected Earth
An overview of the unifying idea of Earth system science; this approach views Earth as an integrated network comprising the lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere; sampling the complex interactions between these realms.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E02 — The Vast Depths of Earth Time
Pondering how the great antiquity of Earth is discovered; the observations that lead to the concept of deep time; in the process, they develop the tools that can read the story in rocks; ending with an analogy that puts human time into perspective.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E03 — Fossil Clocks
Delving into biostratigraphy, the study of fossil sequences in rock strata; its discovery solves the problem of correlating sedimentary strata from different regions; this leads to the geological timescale, initiating a revolution in Earth science.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E04 — Paleontologists as Detectives
How paleontologists interpret fossils to reconstruct the traits and environments of extinct life forms; some of the pitfalls of the field; these include cultural biases that can lead to doubtful conclusions, such as that of the Tyrannosaurus rex.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E01 — The World of Genesis
Considering the nature and scope of biblical archeology; how the Book of Genesis makes its case for the existence of a single God; archeological evidence for a great flood in ancient times; its possible connection to the biblical story of Noah.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E02 — The Tower of Babel
The symbolism of the tower and pyramid in ancient architecture; the Egyptian step pyramid at Saqqara; the Mesopotamian ziggurat's role in religious life and ritual; parallels between the building of ziggurats and the story of the Tower of Babel.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E03 — The Journeys of Abraham
Tracing the life of Abraham from his origins; how Abraham follows the call of God in traveling to Canaan; historical evidence related to the events of Abraham's journey; the narrative of Abraham's search for an heir to his clan and to God's covenant.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E04 — Joseph in Egypt
Archeological traces of Abraham's descendants; the events surrounding Dinah, daughter of Jacob; how their clan is forced to leave Canaan; the story of Joseph's bondage in Egypt; the plausibility of Joseph's rise to the grand vizier to the Pharaoh.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E01 — Earliest History of the Indian Subcontinent
Beginning one's study millions of years ago; plate tectonics shape the subcontinent's mountains, plateaus and river systems; these affect the region's aspects; reviewing South Asia's four macro-regions; how geography guides the course of life.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E02 — Migration and the Adivasi
Three main cultures inhabit the ancient Indian subcontinent; studying the Adivasi, who once comprise the entirety of South Asia's population; how genetic and linguistic analysis shows the Adivasi of 30,000 years ago; their status in India today.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E01 — Exploring the Gift of the Nile
For the ancient Egyptians, the Nile is the source of all life; Egypt's ancient cities and monuments; the rich pantheon of Egyptian gods; the role of Egyptian kings as divine intermediaries; the symbolism of Egyptian architecture, art and ritual.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E02 — The Major Museums of Cairo
Using objects from Cairo's three great museums; tracing 5,000 years of Egyptian history; Narmer Palette sets the conventions for Egyptian art; what a statue of King Khafre and Tutankhamun's golden throne tell about Egypt from various periods.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E01 — Who Are the Celts?
Examining and clarifying common preconceptions about Celtic identity; painting the initial brushstrokes on the canvas of a European culture most widely perceived as Scottish and Irish while promising much more.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E02 — The Celts and the Classical World
Studying the earliest written records of the Celts from Italy, Greece and Spain, dating as far back as the sixth century B.C.; scholarly theories about the Celts' migration throughout Europe; the foundation of humanity's understanding of the Celts.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E01 — The Interconnected Earth

description:

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E01 — Benjamin Franklin and the American Dream
In Franklin's unfinished autobiography, he creates a persona for himself as a role model others may follow; there is more to Franklin than he shows on the page; surveying the book offers some foundational insights into his life and his worldview.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E02 — Meet the Franklins
The Franklins are a typical 18th-century family, extended across space; filled with comedy and tragedy, wealth and poverty; meeting his parents and siblings; learning the story of his wife and firstborn son; accompanying Franklin on his travels.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E01 — The Origins of King Arthur
Studying images of the Arthurian legend and their relationship to historical reality; tracing the history of post-Roman Britain; the large-scale invasions of the Anglo-Saxons; evidence that a single individual rose up to lead his people.

title: King Arthur: History and Legend
description:
S01 E02 — An Arthur-Like Figure in Cornwall
Investigating archeological and historical evidence that supports the existence of an Arthur-like figure in early Britain; studying the site of Cadbury Castle, the center of operations of a leader who thwarted the Saxons; the supposed tomb of Arthur.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E01 — What is a Pirate?
Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E02 — Pirate Facts and Fictions
Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

title: The Decisive Battles of World History
description:
S01 E01 — What Makes a Battle Decisive?
How warfare changes the course of historical events; the factors that make a military battle decisive, such as its role in transfers of power and its social and political effects; the study of battles as an analytical tool for understanding history.

title: The Decisive Battles of World History
description:
S01 E02 — 1274 B.C. Kadesh - Greatest Chariot Battle
The battle of Kadesh ushers in an era of peace in the ancient Near East; the strategy and tactics of the Egyptian and Hittite armies; the unusual sequence of battlefield events that lead to a remarkable treaty; a forerunner of peaceful diplomacy.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E01 — Dawn of the Roman Empire
Setting the stage for Rome's transition from a republic to an empire; Octavian wins a civil war against Mark Antony; he soon achieves what Julius Caesar could not, a one-man rule over Rome.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E02 — Augustus, the First Emperor
Meeting Octavian, who becomes Rome's first emperor; he takes the title of Augustus; gaining control of the military; ruling Rome without inspiring his own assassination; how these are some of history's most astonishing feats.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E03 — Tiberius and Caligula
Despite his achievements, Augustus fails in the key area of choosing a successor; after an almost comical series of events, he secures a male heir to take the throne; witnessing the debacle of Roman leadership under Tiberius and Caligula.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E04 — Claudius and Nero
The succession after Caligula continues to be a problem for the Roman Empire; Claudius, though physically challenged, is a good administrator; Nero is depraved and self-aggrandizing, nearly bankrupting the empire; tracing the story of their rule.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E01 — Exploring How England Came to Be
Seeing what makes Anglo-Saxon England so captivating; a brief survey of the traditional scholarship across the ages; Professor Paxton outlines how to form a picture of the Anglo-Saxons, including written evidence, literary sources and more.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise and Fall of Roman Britain
England is forged in the crucible of the decline of the Romans; exploring the impact of the Romans on Britain, from Hadrian's Wall to the city of London; the role of Christianity, the state of language and the collapsing economy during this time.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E03 — The Germanic Migrations to Britain
The three primary invasions of Germanic people that schoolchildren are aware of; reflecting on the accuracy of this narrative; how varying sources, as well as DNA and archeological evidence, paint a much more complex picture of Germanic migrations.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E04 — The Britons Resist: The Legend of King Arthur
Pondering whether there is resistance among the locals to Germanic migrations; looking at King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table; investigating Arthur's status as a real person, who he is based on and his impact on the history of Britain.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E01 — Cities, Civilizations, and Sources
The different kind of approach one will take in exploring the ancient world; hearing a story that illustrates the risks of letting one's own cultural biases and limited perspective overly influence the interpretation of archeological discoveries.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E02 — From Out of the Mesopotamian Mud
This civilization reveals a theme that appears again and again; grasping the role of geography and resources in shaping Mesopotamia's method of subsistence, religion, structures, empire and means of leaving its written record.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E03 — Cultures of the Ancient Near East
The lack of geographical barriers makes it difficult for the most powerful cities to retain their power; how a succession of empires rise and fall, leaving behind legacies ranging from the use of intimidation in warfare to seafaring and astrology.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E04 — Ancient Egypt - The Gift of the Nile
An introduction to Egypt reveals a civilization shaped by geography: how the Nile's annual flooding, though creating a fertile strip amounting to three percent of Egypt, permits civilization to thrive in an otherwise uninhabitable desert.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E01 — Welcome to Britain
Why Great Britain offers so much as a travel destination; thousand-year-old castles and cathedrals; contemporary art museums and scenic hikes; a look at the scope of all Britain has to offer, along with a few unique ideas.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E02 — Prehistoric Britain
The beginning of Great Britain's history 5,000 years ago; a mysterious ancient people whose only vestiges are earthworks and stone circles; the massive popularity of Stonehenge; visiting other ancient ruins such as Avebury or Maiden Castle.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E03 — Roman Britain
The Roman conquest; how the Romans invaded Great Britain and spread their territory; Hadrian's Wall marking the edge of the empire; the Roman impact on Great Britain, from the city of Bath to the island's long and straight roads.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E04 — Anglo-Saxon and Viking Britain
How a number of Germanic tribes stepped in to fill the power vacuum left after the Romans left Britain; exploring the Anglo-Saxon conquests; the Viking attacks in the Middle Ages; Offa's Dyke and the monastery of Lindisfarne.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E01 — Dawn of the Roman Empire
Setting the stage for Rome's transition from a republic to an empire; Octavian wins a civil war against Mark Antony; he soon achieves what Julius Caesar could not, a one-man rule over Rome.

description:
S01 E02 — Augustus, the First Emperor
Meeting Octavian, who becomes Rome's first emperor; he takes the title of Augustus; gaining control of the military; ruling Rome without inspiring his own assassination; how these are some of history's most astonishing feats.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E03 — Tiberius and Caligula
Despite his achievements, Augustus fails in the key area of choosing a successor; after an almost comical series of events, he secures a male heir to take the throne; witnessing the debacle of Roman leadership under Tiberius and Caligula.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E04 — Claudius and Nero
The succession after Caligula continues to be a problem for the Roman Empire; Claudius, though physically challenged, is a good administrator; Nero is depraved and self-aggrandizing, nearly bankrupting the empire; tracing the story of their rule.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E01 — Exploring How England Came to Be
Seeing what makes Anglo-Saxon England so captivating; a brief survey of the traditional scholarship across the ages; Professor Paxton outlines how to form a picture of the Anglo-Saxons, including written evidence, literary sources and more.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise and Fall of Roman Britain
England is forged in the crucible of the decline of the Romans; exploring the impact of the Romans on Britain, from Hadrian's Wall to the city of London; the role of Christianity, the state of language and the collapsing economy during this time.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E03 — The Germanic Migrations to Britain
The three primary invasions of Germanic people that schoolchildren are aware of; reflecting on the accuracy of this narrative; how varying sources, as well as DNA and archeological evidence, paint a much more complex picture of Germanic migrations.

title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
description:
S01 E04 — The Britons Resist: The Legend of King Arthur
Pondering whether there is resistance among the locals to Germanic migrations; looking at King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table; investigating Arthur's status as a real person, who he is based on and his impact on the history of Britain.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E01 — Cities, Civilizations, and Sources
The different kind of approach one will take in exploring the ancient world; hearing a story that illustrates the risks of letting one's own cultural biases and limited perspective overly influence the interpretation of archeological discoveries.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E02 — From Out of the Mesopotamian Mud
This civilization reveals a theme that appears again and again; grasping the role of geography and resources in shaping Mesopotamia's method of subsistence, religion, structures, empire and means of leaving its written record.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E03 — Cultures of the Ancient Near East
The lack of geographical barriers makes it difficult for the most powerful cities to retain their power; how a succession of empires rise and fall, leaving behind legacies ranging from the use of intimidation in warfare to seafaring and astrology.

title: History of the Ancient World: A Global Perspective
description:
S01 E04 — Ancient Egypt - The Gift of the Nile
An introduction to Egypt reveals a civilization shaped by geography: how the Nile's annual flooding, though creating a fertile strip amounting to three percent of Egypt, permits civilization to thrive in an otherwise uninhabitable desert.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E01 — Welcome to Britain
Why Great Britain offers so much as a travel destination; thousand-year-old castles and cathedrals; contemporary art museums and scenic hikes; a look at the scope of all Britain has to offer, along with a few unique ideas.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E02 — Prehistoric Britain
The beginning of Great Britain's history 5,000 years ago; a mysterious ancient people whose only vestiges are earthworks and stone circles; the massive popularity of Stonehenge; visiting other ancient ruins such as Avebury or Maiden Castle.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E03 — Roman Britain
The Roman conquest; how the Romans invaded Great Britain and spread their territory; Hadrian's Wall marking the edge of the empire; the Roman impact on Great Britain, from the city of Bath to the island's long and straight roads.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E04 — Anglo-Saxon and Viking Britain
How a number of Germanic tribes stepped in to fill the power vacuum left after the Romans left Britain; exploring the Anglo-Saxon conquests; the Viking attacks in the Middle Ages; Offa's Dyke and the monastery of Lindisfarne.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E01 — Dawn of the Roman Empire
Setting the stage for Rome's transition from a republic to an empire; Octavian wins a civil war against Mark Antony; he soon achieves what Julius Caesar could not, a one-man rule over Rome.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E03 — The Native South and Southwest in the 1600s
The cultures that exist before the Spanish Invasion; the struggle for power through Hernando de Soto's entrada through the Southeast; the Pueblo War for Independence in the Southwest; the Native American worlds born in the aftermath of these events.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E04 — Werowocomoco and Montaup in the 1600s
How connections are forged between Native Americans and newcomers as they incorporate each other into their worlds; examples across the Northeastern Woodlands down to Werowocomoco; how the search for common ground begins at first contact.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E05 — Iroquoia and Wendake in the 1600s
Once Europeans arrive, the Native peoples of the Northeast want to maintain their autonomy; the strategies and experiences of the Wendat and Iroquois; Native Americans transform the European colonial project while preserving a measured separatism.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E06 — Indian-European Encounters, 1700-1750
An exploration of the Iroquois Confederacy and the Lenape people; Native Americans keep or lose their lands through treaties and negotiations; the repercussions of these conflicts sometimes go beyond relocation, enslavement or near annihilation.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E07 — The Seven Years' War in Indian Country
The French and Indian War is portrayed in history as a turning point for Native nations in the East; for some, it serves as a victory, for others, a defeat; a changed storyline; the perspectives of Native people who experience the era differently.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E08 — The American Revolution through Native Eyes
The Native Americans experience the American Revolution as allies, as participants in their own civil wars and as neutral parties; for many, the resolution of the American Revolution holds little meaning; the rule of the colonists or the Crown.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E01 — Three Peoples Collide
Neither the Eurocentric term 'discovery' nor the blandly neutral 'encounters' do justice to the impact of Europeans, Africans and Native Americans coming together in the New World; a collision whose causes and effects are outlined in this lecture.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E02 — The Native Americans
Most of the inhabitants of the Americas arrive in migratory waves from Asia between 40,000 and 2,000 B.C.; their civilizations are based on sophisticated irrigation and farming; complex religions and social structures; rivaling those of Europe.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E03 — Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas
The Aztecs and Incas create empires built upon religions of conquest; powered by the control of water, around Lake Texcoco in Mexico and high in the Andes Mountains, respectively; the Maya develops an advanced knowledge of astronomy and mathematics.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E04 — Europeans and Africans
Europe and Africa are connected for centuries by Old World trading networks centered around the Mediterranean; in the 15th century, Spain and Portugal shift the trade out of the Mediterranean and into the Atlantic, along the west coast of Africa.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E05 — European Overseas Expansion
In 1492, Europe is dwarfed in power by the civilizations of China, India, the Ottomans of the Middle East and even the empires of Africa; the modern nation-state, capitalism, Christianity and new technologies combine to catapult Portugal.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E06 — Christopher Columbus-Path to Conquest
Neither villain nor visionary, Christopher Columbus is an extremely learned and devout man; he embarks on his enterprise of the Indies for gold, glory and gospel; he dies unaware that he has initiated arguably the most important event in history.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E07 — Stepping Stones-The Conquest of the Caribbean
Within a generation, the Spanish sweep across the Caribbean Sea and the surrounding regions, conquering and annihilating native peoples, establishing the patterns of conquest that they repeat across the Americas for nearly a century.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E08 — The Rise of Hernán Cortés
In the conquest of Mexico, two empires collide; two mighty figures clash; Hernan Cortes leads a renegade Spanish expedition to the coast of Mexico; he exploits divisions among the various Indian tribes, capturing Montezuma in his own palace.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E01 — The Unknown Story of Ancient North America
Revealing the truths of ancient North America, which include pyramids, state-of-the-art highways and productive innovators; how the societies seemed destined to remain a mystery due to European conquerors and no written records.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The First Human Migrations to the Americas
DNA evidence pointing to Asia as the origin of all human migration to North America; migration passages across the Bering Strait; ancient habitation sites across the continent; why scientists cannot yet agree on the ages of the sites.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E03 — Clovis Man: America's First Culture
Exploring the very first American culture, which is identified by a specialized hunting tool called the Clovis point; how the Clovis populated the Americas from coast to coast; how some of the Clovis people evolved into the last Paleo-Indians.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E04 — The Archaic Period: Diversity Begins
How Paleo-Indian culture began to diversify regionally; understanding why some groups developed a hunting and gathering culture, while others fished from temporary camps; what DNA research reveals about one ancient sedentary people.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E05 — Late Archaic Innovations
How the creative yet disparate peoples of North America developed innovations such as corn agriculture, permanent houses and religion about 5,000 years ago; exploring the only innovation common to these many different cultures.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E06 — Poverty Point: North America's First City
How a group of ancient people developed a planned community on more than 900 acres of land to accommodate 4,000 to 5,000 inhabitants; how the city of Poverty Point functioned for 1,000 years and included one of the world's oldest pyramids.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E07 — Medicine Wheels of the Great Plains
Surveying what is known about medicine wheels, which are wagon-wheel type arrangements of stones on the ground that vary in their number of spokes and size; learning their functions and meaning, which almost certainly changed over time.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E08 — Adena Culture and the Early Woodlands Period
The evolution of the continent's first coherent civilizations in Ohio about 3,000 years ago; studying the Adena, the first ancient American culture with a wide-ranging influence; the Adena's conical burial mounds and shared concept of an afterlife.
